core.title: RED tests carry a guaranteed-fail marker
core.given: A test whose declared phase is RED
core.when: the RED test is written, edited, or scanned by the RED gate
core.then: Each RED test MUST contain at least one accepted guaranteed-fail marker from the stack's accepted marker vocabulary (supplied by the profile).
prefer: Write the behavioral oracle first (required by red-behavioral-assertion): derive it from the bound acceptance's Given/When/Then so it fails because the behavior is not implemented correctly.
Then add one marker after the declared stimulus runs, using one of the stack's accepted guaranteed-fail markers.
Remove the marker in GREEN only once the behavioral assertion carries the proof and passes.
avoid: Using the marker as the only meaningful reason the test is red.
Throwing before the declared stimulus is exercised.
Wrapping a vacuous or already-passing case in the test runner's expected-failure wrapper construct.
Weakening the behavioral assertion because the marker already guarantees failure.
core.why: Failing-first is a runtime property no static check can observe; the marker is the decidable structural proxy. It aids the check; it is not the RED objective or the behavioral oracle. The rule is complementary to red-behavioral-assertion: that rule asks whether the case encodes the missing behavior, while this rule gives the static gate evidence that the artifact is intentionally in RED. A test whose only meaningful reason for failing is an unconditional marker, a throw before the stimulus, or a failing wrapper around an otherwise passing case is mechanically red while the acceptance remains unproven.
evidence: The check finds at least one accepted marker in every RED-phase file; a reviewer confirms each RED case carries one.
The case also contains the behavioral witness required by red-behavioral-assertion.
Running the target case confirms it reaches the intended behavior.
Causal check: apart from the structural marker, the behavioral oracle would still fail for the expected missing-behavior reason without relying on the unconditional marker.
verification: Disposition: strict — a RED-phase file containing none of the accepted markers is a violation; severity 3 in the reference realization.

The check is file-level: it flags a RED-phase file that contains none of the accepted markers anywhere in the file; it does not report per-case absence when another case in the file supplies a marker, even though the obligation is stated per test.
Only RED-phase files are scanned; files declaring GREEN or REFACTOR, files with no declared phase (that is the phase-declared rule's finding), and non-test production source files are out of scope.
The check is exactly the structural proxy: whether a test actually fails first is a runtime property it cannot observe; runtime failure is confirmed by running the case.
The accepted marker list is profile data defining the marker vocabulary; it is not a filter on which test files or languages are in scope.
The stack's expected-failure wrapper constructs are markers, not self-skips; no-self-skip deliberately does not flag them.

values: a RED-phase test file containing none of the accepted guaranteed-fail markers (whole-file result, not per-case)

fires: A test file whose declared phase is RED contains none of the accepted guaranteed-fail markers anywhere in the file.
A test file in any of the stack's languages declares phase RED and contains none of the accepted markers (the marker vocabulary is a construct list, not a language eligibility filter).

A test file whose declared phase is RED contains only behavioral assertions and no accepted marker appears anywhere in the file (the obligation still applies to each case, but this check's finding is file-level).
doesNotFire: A test file whose declared phase is GREEN or REFACTOR.
A test file with no declared phase (that is the phase-declared rule's finding).
A RED case that has a marker but lacks a behavioral witness (that is red-behavioral-assertion's finding, not this marker check's).
Flagging the stack's expected-failure wrapper as a self-skip (no-self-skip deliberately does not flag it).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test runner, by which the test files in scope of the RED gate are recognized (any of its test files, in any of the stack's languages, is in scope).
The stack's accepted guaranteed-fail marker constructs that satisfy the RED marker obligation (the marker vocabulary the gate matches).
profileRequirements.bunValue: `throw new Error('Not implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`, `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, `it.fails(`, `test.failing(`

profileRequirements.meaning: How a test file declares its ATDD phase (RED/GREEN/REFACTOR), which the RED gate reads to select files.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's accepted guaranteed-fail constructs that mark a RED-phase test (the marker vocabulary matched by the RED gate).
proposedKeys.bunValue: `throw new Error('Not implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`, `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, `it.fails(`, `test.failing(`
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No idiom key describes test constructs; the nearest, idiom.error_types, covers how domain and boundary errors are typed and raised, not guaranteed-fail test markers.

proposedKeys.meaning: How a test file declares its ATDD phase (RED/GREEN/REFACTOR), which phase-scoped gates read.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.declaration covers a plan artifact's own URN and urn.binding.<artifact> covers artifact bindings; no existing key describes a test file's phase declaration.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is fully stack-neutral; only its inputs are stack-specific: the accepted marker vocabulary, the phase-declaration syntax, and the runner's expected-failure wrapper spellings. These are supplied by the profile (idiom.red_markers and idiom.phase_declaration are proposed keys; tooling.test_runner exists), with the exact Bun texts preserved in bunOnly and bun.json delivered as the reference example. Detector/validator/finding ids (bun_tester_discipline_detector, red-file-without-red-marker) stay realization details per the notProfileKeys list, and per-rule severity 3 / strict disposition live in core:verification stated exactly as recorded, with no added enforcement semantics. The 'marker vocabulary is not a language filter' point is kept generically in core:verification without naming TypeScript or JavaScript.
